Key NPCs / Factions: Caelestis Academy, Mirt the Merciless, Boatswain Tarto
Key Details (Player):
• [S01] The tower academy where the cadets train, containing the simulation deck, administration, cadet quarters, sky dock, quartermaster's stores, Spelljammer Nexus, and gymnasium
• [S01] Overlooks the Astral Sea and is organized as a layered order of halls, ranks, and thresholds
• [S01] Struck by a coordinated wave of burglaries during the attack on Mirt
• [S03] An arcane device detonated in its simulation chamber, nearly killing a room of cadets
• [S03] Holds a bridge where Mirt keeps his fishbowl, and an infirmary where the injured recover
• [S03] Governs a fleet-intelligence archive locked behind clearance beyond a cadet's star
Overview (Player): Caelestis is the spelljammer academy where the cadets train, a layered machine of halls, ranks, and access permissions overlooking the Astral Sea. Led by Mirt the Merciless, it drills its cadets through simulation and salvage exercise. A wave of thefts continues to spread through the tower, reaching an instructor's own possessions.

Key Details (Player):
• [S01] A room overlooking the Astral Sea where cadets guide miniature spelljamming ships over a floating field
• [S01] The cadets ran their first true helm exercise here under the tension of an ectoplasmic breach elsewhere in the tower
• [S02] Tarto brought Boogie, Gregory, and Bartholomew here to practice, where Saerthe learned his own miniature ship had been stolen
• [S02] Bartholomew's ease at the helm here settled the crew's open spelljammer seat
• [S03] Holds library terminals between the mock helms and Saerthe's cluttered desk
• [S03] Gregory searched its terminals for arcane artillery and runes but was locked out of a fleet-intelligence archive category by his cadet star
Overview (Player): The Spelljammer Nexus is a training chamber at Caelestis overlooking the Astral Sea, where cadets learn to extend mind and magic into a vessel by guiding miniature ships across a floating field.

Key Details (Player):
• [S01] Cluttered chambers of Caelestis's head, scattered with clothes, curiosities, and a fishbowl holding two octopi, Flotsam and Jetsam
• [S01] Contains a wardrobe that opens onto a bounded stretch of astral night with unfamiliar constellations
• [S01] Site of the fight with the centipede creatures released from the delivered crate
Overview (Player): Mirt's quarters are the cluttered, excess-strewn chambers of Caelestis's head, home to a fishbowl of octopi and an impossible wardrobe that opens onto bounded astral night — a magical replica of a place in the Viren star system.

Key Details (Player):
• [S01] Where spelljamming ships of every shape rest beneath the void; Kip and Pik taught the cadets the anatomy of a vessel and the meaning of the helm
• [S01] Boogie noticed a suspicious exchange between a dock officer and a merchant here
• [S02] Casey came here looking for Joffrey, did not find him, and sat at the rail thinking of his brother when the familiar presence settled beside him again
• [S03] Boogie and Sol talked past a security guard, invoking Mirt's name, to trace a crate here
• [S03] They found a crate marked with the rod's symbol tucked behind others, holding something neither living nor hollow
• [S03] Sol learned from a cargo clerk that shipments route through Mr. Blip, with Toril as the nearest destination and Hakatha a secondary stop
Overview (Player): The sky dock is Caelestis's docking bay beneath the void, where spelljamming ships of every shape rest and cadets learn the anatomy of a vessel and the workings of the helm.

Key Details (Player): • [S01] Named by Mirt as the location, beyond Hakatha, that his wardrobe magically replicates; the destination Casey's vision and guiding voice pointed toward
Overview (Player): The Viren star system, beyond a place called Hakatha, is the region Mirt's impossible wardrobe magically replicates. A vision and a guiding voice have pointed Casey toward it as a destination.

Key Details (Player):
• [S02] Caelestis's crowded refectory, packed with cadets of every wildspace people beneath blue-glowing orbs
• [S02] Petty Officer Winston Ryeback runs its kitchen at a carrying bellow
• [S02] Known for its dragon scale pizza and knock-your-mama's-socks-off soup
• [S02] Along the back wall runs a board of handwritten notices — well-wishes, odd jobs, dock requests, and missing-item notices
• [S02] Where the crew first gathered as a table and sorted out their shipboard roles
Overview (Player): The Weeping Goddess is Caelestis's bustling refectory, thronged with cadets from every corner of wildspace beneath blue-glowing orbs. Its kitchen is run by Petty Officer Winston Ryeback, and a back-wall notice board carries odd jobs, dock requests, and missing-item notices.

Key Details (Player):
• [S02] The dock named in a cargo notice Casey pulled from the refectory board
• [S02] Casey confused it with another dock and ended up working cargo for Rindle Gearloft instead
Overview (Player): The Sea Dock is one of Caelestis's docking bays, named on a cargo notice Casey pulled from the refectory board. He meant to work a job here but confused it with a neighboring dock.

Key NPCs / Factions: Saerthe Abizjn, Boatswain Tarto, Caelestis Academy
Key Details (Player):
• [S02] Where both cadet crews were summoned and briefed by Saerthe and Tarto for a salvage race
• [S02] Cadets entered pods here to run the simulation of a hammerhead recovering a logbook from a derelict in an asteroid field
Overview (Player): The Simulation Deck is the chamber at Caelestis where cadets enter pods to run immersive exercises. Here both cadet crews were briefed and set against each other in a salvage race through simulated wildspace.

Key Details (Player):
• [S03] A stone-carved beholder vessel drifting in orbit above Toril, believed abandoned
• [S03] The crew was to install a spelljamming helm on its command deck and use its appearance to move through Hakathan space unchallenged
• [S03] Its interior is stone-floored, dim, and smells old; a lantern-wisp bloom has overrun much of it
• [S03] Clockwork horrors were found feeding on the broken autognome Ostekk-6 in the cargo hold
• [S04] The crew dispatched the clockwork horrors in the cargo hold and cleared the lantern-wisp bloom choking the garden shaft, but found the wisps persisted by some unknown cause
• [S04] A deck below waits reachable only by rope; the crew held to rest before descending, sensing something waiting there
Overview (Player): The tyrant ship is a stone-carved beholder vessel drifting above Toril, believed abandoned when the crew boarded it. They mean to install a helm on its command deck and fly it through Hakathan space unnoticed, but its interior is choked with a lantern-wisp bloom, prowled by clockwork horrors, and said to hide a shape-shifting mimic.

Key Details (Player):
• [S01] Named by Mirt as a place the Viren star system lies beyond
• [S03] A world populated entirely by beholders and their kin, watched by beholder patrols
• [S03] Struck by an adamantine meteor that hit its spire, which the crew was sent to recover
• [S03] Named by a Sky Dock cargo clerk as a secondary destination for certain shipments
Overview (Player): Hakatha is a world populated entirely by beholders and their kin, watched by beholder patrols. An adamantine meteor has struck its spire, and the crew has been sent to recover it — using a tyrant ship's appearance to move through Hakathan space unchallenged.

Key Details (Player):
• [S03] Named by a Sky Dock cargo clerk as the nearest destination on most shipping routes
• [S03] The world above which the abandoned tyrant ship drifts in orbit
Overview (Player): Toril is a world named as the nearest destination on most of the academy's shipping routes. The abandoned tyrant ship the crew boarded drifts in orbit above it.
